jobs.occupation: Researcher in Quaternary Geology and Paleoclimate
jobs.description:
About the position
Starting date as soon as possible. The appointment is a full-time position and is for a period 6 months.

Place of work is Department of Geosciences, Section for Meteorology and Oceanography at Blindern, Oslo Norway.

The position is associated with the NORCLI (Nordic Climate History) project.

NORCLI is an interdisciplinary project led by Prof. Dominik Collet at the Department of Archaeology, Conservation and History and co-lead by Professor Kirstin Krüger at the Department of Geosciences, Section for Meteorology and Oceanography, at the University of Oslo. It is financed by the University of Oslo Thematic Research Group.

NORCLI is investigating Nordic Climate History: What happened the last time Nordic societies encountered rapid climate change? How did natural and social environments interact during the Little Ice Age (1300-1900), also in response to major volcanic events (i.e., 1690s, 1783-1783 Laki)? What can be learned from the ways people adapted to challenges that are in many ways similar to the ones we face today? The Nordic Climate History (NORCLI) research renders these fundamental questions researchable, using a novel 'socionatural' approach that integrates climatology and history and connects them to museology. NORCLI is working in three steps: (1) reconnecting available data from both the archives of nature (lake sediments, tree-rings, ice cores), climate physics (climate model data) and of society (historical records, material culture) with a focus on extreme events initiated by abrupt climate change in the last two millennia; (2) integrating interactions ‘from agriculture to culture’ bringing natural scientists and historians together; and (3) narrating results to a wider museum and societal audience.

The Quaternary Geology and Paleoclimate Researcher is expected to contribute to the working steps (1) and (2). The researcher shall be an experienced independent scientist within quaternary geology and paleoclimate specialized on varved lake sediments and their analyses in the Nordic countries. In addition, expertise on floods, hydroclimate variations, and natural hazards in particular in Norway during the Holocene are expected as well. As the candidate will be working closely with the other NORCLI positions on history, ice cores, tree rings, and climate modelling, we are seeking for a team player with an interdisciplinary background. Previous documented experience with the analyses of varved lake sediments in Norway next to other paleo climate proxies, and the historical archives on climate is required.
What skills are important in this role?
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition of being a leading research faculty. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

Qualification requirements:

• Applicants must hold a degree equivalent to a Norwegian doctoral degree in Paleo Climate. 
• Background in Quaternary geology, paleoclimate and hydroclimate variations during the past 2000 years and Holocene in Norway and other Nordic countries.
• Experience in analyzing varved lake sediments in Norway including field, lab and data work.
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English and Norwegian. 
Desired qualifications:

• The potential to integrate and develop interdisciplinary approaches and to work in multi-disciplinary teams.
Personal skills:

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
• Ability to work precise in a structured manner and swiftly adapts to new tasks
• Good communication and collaboration skills
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal skills.
We need different perspectives in our work 
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
We offer / We can offer you / Why should you choose us?
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment.
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities. 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Researcher, position code 1109 in salary range NOK 650 000 - 850 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.
Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
Application
Your application should include:

• Cover letter (statement of motivation, summarizing scientific work and research interest)
• CV (summarizing education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
• Copies of educational certificates, academic transcript of records 
• A complete list of publications and up to 5 academic works that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee
• Names and contact details of 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and telephone number)
Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
Please note that we are unable to add documentation after the application deadline. As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews.
 
Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.Please refer to  Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and Rules for the use of research posts SKO 1108, 1109, 1110 and 1183 at UiO.

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees to secure the rights to all research results and related intellectual property.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society.

The geosciences are the studies of the planet Earth and its comparative planetology; the atmosphere, the hydrosphere and cryosphere, the Earth's surface and its interior. The Department of Geosciences conducts research and teaching in most of the domains of geoscience; geology, geophysics, physical geography, geomatics, hydrology, meteorology and oceanography. The Department is the broadest geoscience research and education environment in Norway. We perform research at a high international standard and have five ERC (European Research Council) research projects ongoing.

The Department encompasses six scientific sections; Meteorology and Oceanography, Geography and Hydrology, Study of sedimentary basins, Environmental geosciences. and Crustal Processes. We host now a third in the line of three Centre of Excellences:  PHAB – Centre for Planetary Habitability. The Department is also connected to other research centers.The Department aims to contribute to the new and important UN Sustainability Development Goals, and are important contributors to IPCC (UN’s Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change). The staff consists of 40 professors and associate professors, in addition to postdoctoral fellows, PhD students, researchers, technical- and administrative staff. The Department has around 200 employees.

jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i økonomi og finans
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig inntil tre stipendiatstillinger innen samfunnsøkonomi eller finans ved Handelshøgskolen UiS, Avdeling for samfunnsøkonomi og finans. Stillingene er ledige fra 1. september 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

De som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i samfunnsøkonomi. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingene er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.
Forskningstema
Kandidater som ønsker å forske innenfor de områdene i økonomi og finans som er beskrevet nedenfor, oppfordres til å søke. Dette er fagfelt der avdelingen har sterk forskningskompetanse og god veiledningskapasitet. Avdelingen har en sterk vektlegging av empirisk og eksperimentell forskning, med kompetanse som spenner over flere områder innen økonomi og finans. Forskningen innen finans omfatter 

• eksperimentell finans
• prising av finansielle aktiva (asset pricing)
• markedsmikrostruktur
• eierstyring og selskapsledelse (corporate governance).
Innen samfunnsøkonomi omfatter forskningen 

• empirisk og kvantitativ analyse av internasjonal handel, energimarkeder og miljø
• store sosioøkonomiske spørreundersøkelser og eksperimenter om befolkningens preferanser for klima-, natur- og forurensningspolitikk
• felteksperimenter innen arbeids- og utdanningsøkonomi
Én av stipendiatstillingene vil være tilknyttet Synapse Lab. Kandidater som er interessert i denne stillingen, bør angi dette i søknaden og kort forklare hvordan deres forskningsinteresser samsvarer med labens forskningsaktiviteter.

Vi oppfordrer deg til å utforske avdelingens forskningsgrupper  og pågående prosjekter for inspirasjon. 
Prosjektskisse
Som en del av søknaden ber vi deg å inkludere en kort personlig beskrivelse på engelsk der du redegjør for dine planer for doktorgradsstudiet, karrieremål og forskningsinteresser, inkluder mulige forskningsideer. Du kan også nevne faglig ansatte ved Avdeling for samfunnsøkonomi og finans som du ønsker å samarbeide med dersom du blir tatt opp på ph.d.-programmet. Denne beskrivelsen er ikke en fullstendig prosjektbeskrivelse, men vil hjelpe oss til å forstå din motivasjon og faglig retning.

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. 
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor økonomi eller finans eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato.

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.

Dersom du fullfører mastergraden våren 2027, er du også velkommen til å søke.
 
Vi legger også vekt på at du:

• har solide kvantitative og metodiske ferdigheter som er relevante for forskning innen samfunnsøkonomi eller finans, for eksempel innen økonometri, anvendt statistikk eller analytisk modellering
• er motivert for å forske og har potensial som forsker innen fagområdet
• har faglige og personlige forutsetninger for å fullføre doktorgraden innenfor den fastsatte tidsrammen
• tenker nytt og kreativt
• arbeider effektivt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• viser høy faglig integritet og legger stor vekt på kvalitet i arbeidet ditt
• arbeider strukturert og kan håndtere stor arbeidsmengde
• behersker engelsk godt, både skriftlig og muntligKrav til engelskkunnskaper
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig, er en forutsetning for opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet. 

Dersom du er internasjonal søker og ikke omfattes av fritaksordningene nedenfor, må du dokumentere engelskkunnskapene dine med et gyldig resultat fra én av følgende språktester:

• TOEFL – Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT). Minimum resultat: 90/4.5
• IELTS – International English Language Testing Service. Minimum resultat: 6.5
• Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) eller Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) fra Universitetet i Cambridge
• PTE Academic – Pearson Test of English Academic. Minimum resultat: 62
Du er fritatt fra kravet dersom du:

• har fullført minst ett års universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia eller USA
• har fullført en mastergrad med engelsk som undervisningsspråk i et EU-/EØS-land eller i India
• er fritatt i henhold til HK-dirs GSU liste
• ikke inngår i de ovennevnte unntakskategoriene, men har bodd i Norge de siste fem åreneSom stipendiat ved UiS får du
• forskerutdanning ved et universitet med et viktig samfunnsoppdrag
• et ambisiøst og inkluderende forskningsmiljø
• veiledning og støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling
• gratis norskkurs dersom du ikke behersker norsk, svensk eller dansk på minimum A2-nivå ved ansettelse
• tilgang til Lifekeys, en digital tjeneste for mental helse og livskvalitet
• lønn som stipendiat etter Statens lønnsregulativ i stillingskode 1017, kr 580.000 brutto pr år, med lønnsutvikling etter ansiennitet i stillingen. 
• medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse med gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Les mer om ansattgoder og fordeler på uis.no.
Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  
Slik søker du
Søk stillingen ved å klikke på "Søk stillingen" på denne siden. 

I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

• en kort personlig redegjørelse der du beskriver planene dine for doktorgradsstudiet, karrieremålene dine og forskningsinteressene dine
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• Legg ved referanser, attester, vitnemål og annen dokumentasjon du mener er relevant. Hvis du har tatt en standardisert test som GRE eller GMAT, ber vi deg legge ved testresultatene.
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd
• publikasjoner eller annet relevant forskningsarbeid
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 1.900 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet.Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjente.

Handelshøgskolen UiS tilbyr bachelorutdanninger i økonomi og administrasjon og rettsvitenskap. I tillegg tilbys master i økonomi og administrasjon (siviløkonomutdanning), rettsvitenskap, regnskap og revisjon, erfarings-basert masterprogram rettet mot næringslivet (EMBA) samt forskerutdanning (PhD). Fakultetet legger til rette for utdanning, forskning og formidling innenfor en stor spennvidde av fag, som finans, markedsføring, organisasjon og ledelse, regnskap og revisjon, rettsvitenskap, strategi og økonomi. Universitetets Senter for innovasjonsforskning og Senter for entreprenørskap er organisatorisk plassert ved fakultetet. Pr i dag er omlag 120 ansatte og 1.400 studenter tilknyttet fakultetet. Handelshøgskolen ved UiS er organisert i tre avdelinger: Avdeling for innovasjon, ledelse og markedsføring, Avdeling for regnskap og rettsvitenskap og Avdeling for samfunnsøkonomi og finans.

jobs.occupation: Researcher in Biometric Security and Anti-Fraud Technologies
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWHqR5i1FHE&feature=youtu.beAbout the Job
The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU Gjøvik has a vacancy for a Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems. 

The position is for an intended period of 24 months and is part of SAFE – Secure Anti-Fraud Excellence Center, funded by Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark and SpareBank 1 Østlandet in collaboration with NTNU and industry partners.The researcher will be a key member of WP1 and lead its socio-technical analysis of financial fraud, hosted at CCIS, NTNU Gjøvik. WP1 examines vishing and safe-account fraud and a proposed extension to investment fraud. It distinguishes technical authentication and payment confirmation from legally valid consent.

The research reconstructs how fraud unfolds across channels, while focusing detection and intervention on evidence actually visible to the bank between customer authentication and payment authorisation. Off-bank calls, screen sharing and remote-access activities are described where case sources support them, but are not assumed to be observable by the bank.

The work draws on public decisions of Finansklagenemnda, court judgments, and anonymised or otherwise lawfully accessible cases from SAFE’s banking partners. Results feed into cognitive experiments (WP2), detection research (WP3), scientific publications and a policy white paper.Center for Cyber and Information Security (CCIS) at NTNU will host the SAFE Project.Your immediate leader is head of department.
Duties of the position
• Build a systematically coded corpus of fraud cases from public decisions and lawfully accessible bank material, using a shared template and a cross-channel timeline.
• Develop evidence-based fraud scripts for vishing and safe-account fraud and, subject to scope confirmation, investment fraud, including interim inputs for WP2.
• Map each fraud stage, the channels involved, signs of real-time guidance, and what is actually observable by the bank between authentication and payment authorisation.
• Identify legitimate customer activities with similar bank-visible patterns, to support realistic false-alarm testing without using victim characteristics as automatic detection features.
• Study intervention points and fraudster adaptation, including cases where the bank suspects fraud but the customer rejects warnings; help plan a tabletop session with a banking partner.
• Analyse legal, ethical and governance conditions for collecting, using and sharing fraud-related signals, including privacy, bank confidentiality and interbank cooperation.
• Examine the conditions for transaction warnings, delays, refusals and escalation, with attention to customer consent, liability and loss allocation.
• Assess payee verification and, in investment-fraud cases, checks of providers against Finanstilsynet’s register and market warnings; distinguish these from bank-account verification.
• Provide fraud scripts and realistic look-alike scenarios to WP2 and observability findings, intervention points and lawful-signal constraints to WP3.
• Prepare WP1 deliverables, scientific publications and a policy white paper, and present findings to the SAFE Advisory Board and project partners.
• Contribute, where relevant, to SAFE continuing education (EVU), project reporting and research proposal development.Required selection criteria
• A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) or a PhD in information security, socio-technical systems, criminology, information systems, law and technology, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience with systematic analysis of qualitative material, such as case files, legal decisions, interviews or incident reports, using a coding scheme or structured method.
• Knowledge of social engineering and fraud in digital channels, such as vishing, authorised push payment fraud or investment fraud.
• Understanding of digital banking and payment processes, including authentication, payment initiation and customer interaction channels.
• Ability to recognise legal, ethical and data-protection questions and work with relevant specialists on their implications for fraud prevention research.
• Reading comprehension of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language sufficient to analyse Norwegian case material and legal decisions.
• Good written and spoken English and the ability to prepare clear, well-structured research reports.Preferred selection criteria
• A PhD in a relevant field, or research experience after completion of the master’s degree.
• Experience in applied research projects involving banks, financial crime specialists or regulatory and legal experts.
• Experience in crime script analysis, situational crime prevention, socio-technical analysis, or process and threat modelling.
• Knowledge of Norwegian or EU rules on payment services, data protection, bank confidentiality or financial crime prevention.
• Experience in fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, compliance or incident handling in the financial sector.
• Experience in planning and facilitating interviews, workshops or tabletop exercises with practitioners.
• Relevant scientific publications or reports on fraud, cybercrime or socio-technical security.
• Skills in structuring and analysing data, for example using Python, R or NVivo.
• Spoken Norwegian or another Scandinavian language for cooperation with partner banks.Personal characteristics
• Highly motivated for applied and collaborative research with financial-sector partners.
• Analytical, structured and precise in the handling of research evidence and sources.
• Discreet and reliable in handling confidential case material and working across disciplines.
• Self-driven, communicative and able to deliver to agreed deadlines.
• Personal suitability will be emphasized.We offer
• Exciting and stimulating research tasks in a strong international academic environment
• Active collaboration with leading industrial and research partners in Norway and abroad.
• A professional and inclusive work environment.
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Employee benefits at NTNUSalary and conditions
As a researcher (code 1108/1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 580 000– NOK 750 000 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU. 

The intended appointment period is 24 months. Starting date at the latest: 1st April 2027.  Please note that loss of external funding is considered equivalent to loss of work assignments, see §19 (1) of the public Employees act. In the event of dismissal by the employer, the notice period is according to §22 (1) of the Public Employers Act. 

It is a prerequisite that you can be present at and accessible to the institution on a daily basis. After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.
About the application
Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. 

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in  English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your application must include:

• Motivation letter describing your interest in SAFE and socio-technical research on financial fraud (maximum one page).
• CV and relevant certificates.
• Transcripts, diplomas and diploma supplements for completed degrees (BSc, MSc and, where applicable, PhD).
• Master’s thesis or equivalent substantial research work, plus up to three other relevant scientific publications or reports.
• A short statement (1–2 pages) explaining your experience with case-based analysis and how you would map a fraud scenario across channels, distinguish bank-visible evidence from external context, and identify legal or ethical constraints.
• Names and contact information of at least two referees.
It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for  documentation of your competence.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.
General information
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.   

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.  

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. 

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. 

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Prof. Raghavendra Ramachandra, email: raghavendra.ramachandra@ntnu.no . If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact HR Katrine Rennan, e-mail: katrine.rennan@ntnu.no .

Application deadline: 31.12.2026.

Gjøvik is historically an industrial city linked to its location by Lake Mjøsa. Today, the region is known for high-tech companies that supply products to the automotive industry, the defense sector and international markets, among others. NTNU collaborates with many sectors, both in the private sector and public enterprises and services in information security, technology, design, logistics and health.

The city is large enough to have an active and varied cultural offer, safe local communities with kindergartens, schools and sports. It is easy to seek out nature for activities both summer and winter. 

 

 

Om arbeidsgiveren:

NTNU - knowledge for a better world

The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) creates knowledge for a better world and solutions that can change everyday life.

Department of Information Security and Communication Technology

Research is vital to the security of our society. We teach and conduct research in cyber security, information security, communications networks and networked services. Our areas of expertise include biometrics, cyber defence, cryptography, digital forensics, security in e-health and welfare technology, intelligent transportation systems and malware. The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology is one of seven departments in the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering .
